newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani stocks end lower, off day's high.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani stocks end lower, off day's high.

text.p: Pakistani stocks ended lower, off day's high, on Friday after Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz announced an economic reforms package slashing taxes and providing other benefits to boost industrial production and exports, dealers at the Karachi Stock Exchange said.
"The market seems to have over-reacted to the package," said dealer Zubair Ellahi. Stock prices are likely to remain depressed in the next week after the Saturday-Sunday weekend.
Dealer Ali Husain Rajabali said: "The main reason behind the fall was overbought positions and selling of GDR-related stocks, including (telecom utility) PTCL and Hub Power."

The Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) 100-share index ended 17.55 points lower at 1,598.94 amid 49 losers and 13 gainers in a turnover of 17 million shares in an afternoon special session after the package announcement. In the first session, the index closed 3.11 points, or 0.19 percent, up at 1,616.49 amid 116 gainers and 104 losers.
